Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. The CME structure is complex, and in COR2 two fronts to the NE are observed, with a brighter core following the more faint, outer leading edge that matches with the brightest outer feature in CCOR-1. As such, this fit encompasses that outermost leading edge in COR2A with CCOR-1's leading edge.

GOES CCOR-1 only shock analysis, somewhat speculative due to the asymmetric shape and poor visibility. The shock may be visible in STEREO A COR2, but is either too faint or obscured by the bright bulk, and does not track well with the more clear shock front observed in GOES CCOR-1. As such, single spacecraft is used with the same longitude as the LE to approximate, and parameters could vary as a result.

data.note: This CME is visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 before a data gap, to the NW in GOES CCOR-1, and as a halo with the bulk portion directed to the W/NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source for this CME is a long duration M1.6 flare from Active Region 14507 (N04W88) as seen in SDO/AIA 131 with associated moving/opening field lines visible in SDO/AIA 193, 171, and GOES SUVI 284. Other source features include an EUV wave best seen in SDO/AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284, brightening in STEREO A EUVI 304, and dimming in STEREO A EUVI 195. Post eruptive arcades are visible in all main wavelengths from SDO/AIA, GOES SUVI, and STEREO A EUVI. These various source features are visible starting as early as 2026-08-21T09:00Z through 2026-08-21T12:12Z.

Field line opening and Westward moving dimming is seen in SDO AIA 193 in association with this flare, likely suggesting Westward deflection.

data.note: First of three overlapping CMEs in close succession to the NW in STEREO A COR, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1; including CME: 2026-08-25T08:09Z and CME: 2026-08-25T09:09Z. The source is far-sided from Earth, visible in GOES SUVI 284 as field line movement over the NW limb starting as early as 2026-08-25T04:22Z. In STEREO A EUVI 195 three eruptive sources near its NW limb are observed in close succession corresponding to the overlapping CMEs: a brightening at 2026-08-25T05:55Z, a wide spread area of dimming starting around 2026-08-25T06:45Z, and a second brightening starting at 2026-08-25T07:35Z; this CME entry likely corresponds to the first one at 2026-08-25T05:55Z.

data.note: CME observed to the E in STEREO A COR2 and SE in GOES CCOR-1, not yet in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a DSN gap. The source is a filament eruption spanning approximately ~S05E20 to ~N05E13, centered ~N03E18, and an associated C4.7 flare peaking at 2026-08-25T12:58Z observed in SDO AIA 131; nearby but not associated with AR 14513. Observed as the filament ejecta and brightening in SDO AIA 304 and field line movement, dimming, and brief post-eruptive arcade in SDO AIA 171/193. Also seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 as the filament ejecta at 2026-08-25T12:45Z over its east limb. Significantly overlaps with prior CME: 2026-08-25T10:38Z from AR 14513.

The source is possibly related to some brightening along a filament channel (N12W00) between AR 14513 and AR 14517. This CME partially overlaps with outflow following CME: 2026-08-25T10:38Z and CME: 2026-08-25T12:53Z.

The filament eruption is seen near the NW limb in STA EUVI 304.

data.note: CME observed as a full halo to the NE in GOES CCOR-1, and to the W/NW in STEREO A COR2 with a partial halo shock. Not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 real-time due to a DSN gap. The source is far-sided, and may be former AR 14507 expected to be around N05 and W170-W180 at this time. The eruption is only observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 after a data gap ends at 2026-08-27T18:45Z as brightening and post-eruptive arcades over its west limb (limb around W158.3, with STEREO A at W68.3), and in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 as an EUV wave visible over the north and west limbs starting around 2026-08-27T17:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. The CME structure is complex, and in COR2 two fronts to the NE are observed, with a brighter core following the more faint, outer leading edge that matches with the brightest outer feature in CCOR-1. As such, this fit encompasses that outermost leading edge in COR2A with CCOR-1's leading edge.

GOES CCOR-1 only shock analysis, somewhat speculative due to the asymmetric shape and poor visibility. The shock may be visible in STEREO A COR2, but is either too faint or obscured by the bright bulk, and does not track well with the more clear shock front observed in GOES CCOR-1. As such, single spacecraft is used with the same longitude as the LE to approximate, and parameters could vary as a result.
